meta.title: Glossary: technology terms in precise language
meta.description: Clear definitions of the terms we use: Forward Deployed Engineering, RAG, MLOps, Zero Trust, FinOps, high availability and more. One sentence first, no filler jargon.

header.title: Glossary
header.subtitle: The vocabulary of engineering, without the smoke.
header.intro: We define the terms that show up in our work with the same precision we bring to our code, each one explained in a single sentence first, no filler jargon.

terms.short: An elite engineer who embeds inside the client’s business (its context, data and constraints) and owns a problem end to end, rather than writing code at a distance.
terms.body: Palantir originated the model (internally they call them “Deltas”) to solve problems no off-the-shelf product could. In 2026, OpenAI and Anthropic institutionalized it with billions in capital. AXENOR runs it as an elite boutique firm.

terms.short: A model where a vendor supplies “hands” that work under your direction: you still own the problem, the architecture, the risk and the job of coordinating everyone.
terms.body: It contrasts with the Forward Deployed model, where the vendor takes on the whole problem and answers for the final metric, not for billed hours.

terms.short: A collaboration model with a team in a nearby, time-zone-compatible country, enabling real-time work versus the lag of distant offshore.
terms.body: For U.S. clients, Colombia runs on U.S. Eastern Time (ET) and shares the working window, without the friction of the 10-12 hour gap of traditional offshore.

terms.short: The leap from a proof of concept that works in a controlled setting to a system that runs reliably, measurably and maintainably inside the real business.
terms.body: It’s where most technology initiatives stall, AI included: 88% of companies use it, yet few pilots reach production or measure their impact.

terms.short: A technique that connects a language model to your own sources, so it answers with data retrieved from them (with citations) instead of only its training memory.
terms.body: It reduces hallucinations and enables verifiable answers over private documentation, without retraining the model.

terms.short: A set of practices to version, deploy, monitor and retrain machine-learning models in production reproducibly, what DevOps does for software, applied to models.
terms.body: It’s what holds a model up over time: without MLOps, an AI pilot quietly degrades the moment the data shifts.

terms.short: AI systems that carry out multi-step tasks autonomously (deciding, calling tools and acting) rather than just answering a question.
terms.body: In production they require guardrails (action limits), traceability and scoped tasks; without those, autonomy becomes risk.

terms.short: A security model that trusts no user, device or network by default (not even inside the perimeter) and verifies every access explicitly and continuously.
terms.body: It replaces the notion of a “safe internal network” with least-privilege applied to every request.

terms.short: A controlled exercise in which specialists attack your systems, with the owner’s consent, to find real vulnerabilities before an attacker does.
terms.body: Unlike an automated scan, it assesses how weaknesses chain together in a realistic attack.

terms.short: The process of reducing a system’s attack surface: closing unnecessary ports and services, applying least privilege and configuring securely by default.
terms.body: It’s preventive security: fewer things exposed means fewer things an attacker can exploit.

terms.short: A platform that centralizes and correlates logs from across the infrastructure to detect and alert on suspicious activity in near real time.
terms.body: It’s the nervous system of a SOC: it turns millions of scattered events into actionable signals.

terms.short: The function (team, processes and tools) that continuously monitors, detects and responds to security incidents, around the clock.
terms.body: It isn’t a product you install: it’s a practice you operate, and the risk you don’t monitor is the one that ends up costing you.

terms.short: The practice of defining and provisioning infrastructure (servers, networks, cloud) through versioned code files instead of configuring it by hand.
terms.body: It makes deployments repeatable and auditable: the same code produces the same environment, with no surprises.

terms.short: Automation of the path from code to production: every change is tested (continuous integration) and deployed (continuous delivery) frequently and reliably.
terms.body: It shortens the loop between writing a change and seeing it in production, lowering the risk of each release.

terms.short: A discipline that brings financial accountability to cloud spend: giving real-time cost visibility and optimizing it without sacrificing performance.
terms.body: Migrating to the cloud without FinOps tends to relocate the mess into a higher bill; with it, workloads cost what they should.

terms.short: Designing a system to keep running despite component failures, through redundancy and automatic failover, minimizing downtime.
terms.body: It’s measured in “nines” of uptime (for example, 99.99%); when operations rest on the platform, availability is the norm, not the exception.

terms.short: A documented set of procedures to restore systems and data after a major incident (an attack, a major failure, a physical disaster) within an agreed time and data-loss target.
terms.body: It defines two key goals: the RTO (how long recovery takes) and the RPO (how much data can be lost).

terms.short: A strategy to modernize a legacy system gradually: new pieces are built around the old one and traffic is redirected to them over time, replacing it without a single big rewrite.
terms.body: It allows migration with no outage windows and none of the risk of a “big bang” cutover that halts operations.

terms.short: A measurable commitment between a provider and a client on the level of service (availability, response times) that will be met, with defined metrics and consequences.
terms.body: A serious SLA is reported and met; without measurement, it’s a brochure promise.

terms.short: The ability to understand a system’s internal state from its outputs (metrics, logs and traces) to diagnose problems, including ones you didn’t anticipate.
terms.body: It goes beyond monitoring: it doesn’t just tell you something failed, it lets you ask why.
